main_text.l: ti possit, vt Cicero testatur. Imo Christus
ipse dicit, Matt. 12. Omne regnum diuisum
aduersus sese desolatur, & omnis ciuitas aut
domus diuisa aduersus seipsam, non stabit.
in die frigoris, & litigiosa mulier comparan-
tur. Ne sint ergo mulieres litigiosae, sed man-
suetae: neque sint viri aduersus illas amaru-
lenti, sed lenes & patientes: & Deus pacis
omnisque consolationis aderit illis in Chri-

l.i: odium nupta mereatur: ne stupro pollua-
tur in sua virginitate, neue in domo pa-
terna fiat grauida: ne quando viro
iuncta faciat flagitium, aut ne in matrimo-
da custodiam adhibe, ne te ridiculum fa-
ciat inimicis, ciuitatiq; fabulam, ne fa-
mosum in populo, neue in vulgus reddat
nec inter mulieres desideas: nam ut ti-

page.notes: The first word is a woodcut initial, a decorated F, and I read it as "Filia" with a [?] because the letter is ornate. "ciuitatiq;" is a doubtful abbreviation; the q-mark is read from a small scan. The word "sterilescat" is printed with a long s, transcribed as a plain s. The line "nam ut ti-" continues on the following line as "nea", giving "ti-nea" with its printed hyphen.
